title: Night Driving & Bad Weather
whatItIs: Darkness, rain, ice, fog, wind and low sun cut visibility or grip. The answer: see and be seen, slow down and leave far bigger gaps.

keyFacts.text: You MUST use headlights at night, except on roads with lit street lights.

keyFacts: Night (the hours of darkness) runs from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise.

keyFacts.text: You MUST use headlights when visibility is seriously reduced: generally when you can't see beyond 100 m.
You MUST NOT use fog lights unless visibility is seriously reduced, and MUST switch them off when it improves.

keyFacts: Dazzled by oncoming headlights or bright sunlight? Slow down and, if necessary, stop.

keyFacts.text: Before driving in snow or ice you MUST clear all windows and keep lights clean and number plates legible.

a.label: Fog lights
points: Only when visibility is seriously reduced
Can dazzle others and hide your brake lights

b.label: Dipped headlights
points: At night in built-up areas and in dull daytime weather
MUST be used when visibility is seriously reduced

onTheTest.question: Your pupil switched on the rear fog lights in thick fog. Visibility has now improved to well over 100 metres. What must they do?
options: Leave them on until the end of the journey
Switch to the front fog lights only
Use the hazard warning lights instead
onTheTest.why: Rule 236: you MUST NOT use fog lights unless visibility is seriously reduced, and you MUST switch them off when it improves. They dazzle others and can hide brake lights.

onTheTest.question: On an icy road, how much longer can stopping distances be than on a dry road?
options: No longer if the car has ABS
onTheTest.why: Rules 126 and 230: on icy roads the gap should be up to ten times greater, because stopping distances can be ten times greater than on dry roads.

traps: In fog, rear lights ahead give a false sense of security: keep a safe distance.
On ice, tyres make virtually no noise: light, unresponsive steering may mean you're losing grip.
Don't wear tinted glasses, lenses or visors at night or in poor visibility if they restrict your vision.
Queuing at night? Use the parking brake and release the footbrake once traffic behind has stopped.
